title: 2026-11-05_BRICKSTORM_Backdoor_Investigation_a55
description: Investigate and respond to a BRICKSTORM backdoor infection on a Linux system.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are an incident responder tasked with investigating a suspected BRICKSTORM backdoor infection on a Linux system. Your goal is to identify the malicious activity, contain the threat, and remove it from the system.

The BRICKSTORM backdoor is a sophisticated 64-bit ELF executable written in Go. It uses advanced techniques such as SOCKS proxying, multi-layered web service communication, and varied command execution to evade detection. The backdoor also employs DoH, nested TLS encryption, and abuses a legitimate cloud service for command and control (C2) communication.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
Access the target system using the provided credentials and perform an initial investigation to identify any suspicious services or processes. Enter 'start' to begin.

Username: cyrano
Password: Cyrano123!

SSH into the target system using the provided credentials:

```
ssh cyrano@192.168.50.5
```

Once logged in, list all running services to identify any suspicious activity:

```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

Look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names, descriptions, or startup behaviors.

levels.title: Suspicious C2 Service Discovery
levels.content: Security monitoring has detected an unusual network-facing component on the compromised host. Investigate the running services and identify the service responsible for the suspicious activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all services to identify any suspicious activity:

```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

2. Investigate the suspicious service by checking its status and configuration:

```
systemctl status updatemgr.service
systemctl cat updatemgr.service
```

3. Identify the service name responsible for the suspicious activity.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl` command to list all services and look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the status of the suspicious service using `systemctl status <service_name>`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is named `updatemgr.service`. Check its configuration using `systemctl cat updatemgr.service`.

levels.title: C2 Communication Discovery (Port)
levels.content: An unfamiliar network service appears to be involved in unauthorized communication with an external system. Investigate the service and determine the network port associated with this communication.
levels.solution:
1. List all services to identify any suspicious activity:

```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
```

2. Investigate the suspicious service by checking its status and configuration:

```
systemctl status updatemgr.service
systemctl cat updatemgr.service
```

3. Identify the network port associated with the suspicious service by examining the `ExecStart` command in the service configuration.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Use the `systemctl` command to list all services and look for any unfamiliar or suspicious service names.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Check the status of the suspicious service using `systemctl status <service_name>`.

hints.title: Third hint title
hints.content: The suspicious service is named `updatemgr.service`. Check its configuration using `systemctl cat updatemgr.service` and look for the port number in the `ExecStart` command.

levels.title: Suspicious Data Collection Service Discovery
levels.content: System information appears to be collected automatically without an authorized administrative purpose. Investigate the host and identify the service responsible for this activity.
levels.solution:
1. List all services and timers to identify any suspicious activity:

```
systemctl list-units --type=service --all
systemctl list-timers --all
```

2. Investigate the suspicious service by checking its status, configuration, and logs:

```
systemctl status local-inventory.service
systemctl cat local-inventory.service
journalctl -u local-inventory.service
```

3. Identify the service name responsible for the suspicious data collection activity.
